# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 19 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 19 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_019_page_001.jpg

---

**1** But wrath without mercy came upon the ungodly to the very end; for God foreknew what they would yet do —

**2** how, having themselves permitted the departure and sent the Israelites forth with urgency, they would repent and pursue them.

**3** For while they were still engaged in mourning and lamenting at the graves of the dead, they conceived another foolish plan, and pursued as fugitives those whom they had driven out with entreaties.

**4** For the fate they deserved was drawing them to this end, and it made them forget what had happened, so that they might fill up the gap still left in their punishment by further torments.

**5** Thus your people might journey through the water by a miraculous way, while they themselves met a strange death.

**6** For the whole of creation, in its proper order, was being refashioned anew, serving your distinct commands, so that your children might be kept unharmed.

**7** The cloud was seen overshadowing the camp, and dry land appeared where water had been before; out of the Red Sea an unobstructed road, and a grassy plain out of the raging flood —

**8** and the whole nation crossed through, protected by your hand, beholding your marvelous wonders.

**9** For they grazed like horses, and they skipped like lambs, praising you, O Lord, who had delivered them.

**10** For they still remembered what had happened in their sojourn: how the land brought forth gnats instead of cattle, and the river swarmed with frogs instead of fish.

**11** But afterward they saw also a new kind of bird, when, led on by appetite, they requested fancy food,

**12** for quails came up from the sea for their nourishment.

**13** And the punishments came upon the sinners not without prior warnings given through the violence of thunder; for they suffered justly in keeping with their own wickedness, since they had shown a more bitter hatred toward strangers.

**14** For some had merely refused to receive strangers they had never met, but these others had enslaved guests who were their benefactors.

**15** And not only this; but there will be some particular reckoning for those others, since they received strangers with hostility — whereas the Sodomites were hostile to those who had come to them as guests.

**16** But these Egyptians, after welcoming the Israelites with celebrations and granting them equal rights as fellow-residents, later afflicted them with terrible hardships.

**17** And they were struck with blindness, as were also those at the door of the righteous man — when each of them, wrapped in impenetrable darkness, searched for the way through his own doorway.

**18** For the elements shifted places with one another, just as on a harp the notes vary the character of the melody while the rhythm is preserved throughout; and that is something that may be accurately reckoned from the observation of what took place.

**19** For land creatures became water creatures, and swimming creatures transferred themselves to dry land.

**20** Fire maintained its power within water, and water forgot its characteristic quenching force.

**21** On the other hand, flames did not scorch the flesh of perishable creatures moving about among them, nor did they dissolve the easily-melted, ice-like kind of heavenly nourishment.

**22** For in all things, O Lord, you exalted and glorified your people, and did not fail to assist them at every time and place.
